topics.title: override checks the signature
topics.body: Writing `override` makes a mismatch a compile error instead of a silently separate function that never gets called.

topics.title: An abstract class cannot be instantiated
topics.body: A class with a pure virtual function is a contract: only derived classes that implement it can be created.

topics.title: A base pointer calls the derived override
topics.body: Dispatch follows the object’s real type, so the same call runs different code depending on what the pointer refers to.

topics.title: A virtual destructor frees the derived part
topics.body: Deleting through a base pointer only runs the derived destructor when the base destructor is virtual.

topics.title: dynamic_cast checks the real type
topics.body: A failed pointer cast returns null, so the program can branch instead of invoking undefined behaviour.

topics.title: operator== compares values
topics.body: A free comparison function keeps both operands const and returns a plain bool.

topics.title: operator+= reuses operator+
topics.body: Implementing the compound form first and building `+` from it avoids duplicating the arithmetic.

topics.title: Prefix and postfix differ in signature
topics.body: The postfix form takes a dummy int so the compiler can tell the two overloads apart.

topics.title: A friend can see private members
topics.body: A friend declaration grants one function access without making it a member, which is common for stream operators.

topics.title: A conversion operator converts outward
topics.body: It lets an object be used where another type is expected, and `explicit` keeps that conversion from happening silently.

topics.title: Template deduction reads the call
topics.body: The compiler infers `T` from the argument types, so the caller rarely writes the angle brackets.

topics.title: A class template can default its parameter
topics.body: A default argument makes the common instantiation shorter while still allowing another type.

topics.title: A variadic template counts its arguments
topics.body: A fold expression over a parameter pack can consume any number of arguments without recursion.

topics.title: if constexpr drops the other branch
topics.body: The discarded branch is not instantiated, so template code can mention operations that only exist for some types.

topics.title: A template can be specialized
topics.body: A full specialization replaces the generic definition for one concrete type, which is how behaviour is customized.

topics.title: vector grows geometrically
topics.body: When capacity runs out the vector allocates a larger block and moves the elements, so repeated pushes stay amortized constant.

topics.title: map operator[] inserts a default
topics.body: Reading a missing key with `[]` creates it with a zero value, which is convenient for counters and dangerous for lookups.

topics.title: set rejects duplicates
topics.body: Inserting an existing key changes nothing and reports that no insertion happened.

topics.title: deque pushes at both ends
topics.body: A double-ended queue keeps fast insertion at the front and the back, which a vector cannot do at the front.

topics.title: priority_queue pops the largest
topics.body: The default comparator is `less`, so the top is the greatest element and each pop removes it.

topics.title: find_if takes a predicate
topics.body: It returns the first iterator whose element satisfies the predicate, or `end()` when none does.

topics.title: lower_bound needs sorted input
topics.body: It binary-searches for the first element not less than the value, which is why an unsorted range gives a meaningless answer.

topics.title: remove_if moves the kept values
topics.body: It partitions the range and returns the new logical end; erasing that tail is a separate step.

topics.title: A lambda can capture by reference
topics.body: A reference capture lets the lambda update the caller’s variable, which is how a loop accumulates through an algorithm.

topics.title: reverse reorders in place
topics.body: It swaps from both ends toward the middle, so no extra storage is needed.

topics.title: Stack unwinding runs destructors
topics.body: When an exception leaves a scope, every constructed local is destroyed before the handler runs, which is how locks and files are released.

topics.title: what() explains a standard exception
topics.body: Every standard exception derives from `std::exception` and carries a message through `what()`.

topics.title: noexcept keeps moves cheap
topics.body: A move constructor marked `noexcept` lets a vector move elements instead of copying them when it grows.

topics.title: try blocks can nest
topics.body: An inner handler can deal with one failure and let the rest propagate to the outer handler.

topics.title: catch(...) takes anything
topics.body: The ellipsis handler catches every type, which is useful as a last resort but hides the actual exception.

topics.title: ofstream truncates by default
topics.body: Opening an existing file in the default mode clears it, which is why a read-back shows only the new content.

topics.title: ios::app keeps existing content
topics.body: Append mode writes at the end instead of clearing the file, which is how logs survive a restart.

topics.title: Binary mode writes raw bytes
topics.body: Binary mode avoids newline translation, so a struct’s bytes read back exactly as they were written.

topics.title: filesystem::exists checks a path
topics.body: It asks the operating system whether the path resolves, which is the guard before opening a file for reading.

topics.title: remove deletes a file
topics.body: `std::filesystem::remove` returns whether a file was actually removed, so the caller can report a real failure.
